title: Two task queues that honour one contract

blocks.text: In concurrent code, a client must be able to swap one thread-safe queue for another without changing its assumptions. The page's `TaskQueue` contract is:

items: `offer(item)` adds the item and returns `true`, or **returns `false`** when it cannot accept it; it does not throw when full;
`poll()` returns and removes the head, or **returns `null`** when the queue is empty;
`size()` is the current count, and `isEmpty()` says whether it is 0;
both reject a `null` item **the same way**, with `NullPointerException`.

blocks.text: In `Queues`, write both implementations and a client:

items: `BoundedTaskQueue(capacity)`: `offer` returns `false` when it is at capacity (valid per the contract). The page backs it with an `ArrayBlockingQueue`;

`UnboundedTaskQueue`: `offer` always returns `true`, however many items it holds (also valid: it exceeds the minimum guarantee). The page backs it with a `ConcurrentLinkedQueue` for thread safety; the tests here check the contract only;
`drainAll(queue)`, written against `TaskQueue` only, takes every item, head first.

blocks.text: The tests use one thread, so they check the contract's answers, not thread safety: which backing queue you pick for that, and whether `drainAll` polls until `null` or counts `size()` first, is not graded.
A bounded queue of capacity 2 accepts `"a"` and `"b"` and answers `false` for `"c"`.

cases.says: Both queues take 1000, 2000, 3000 and drain them in that order.
A bounded queue at capacity answers false for the next item, without throwing.
poll() on an empty queue returns null, for both queues.
offer(null) throws NullPointerException on both queues.
An unbounded queue accepts 100 000 items, each offer returning true.
offer on a full bounded queue answers false at once, without waiting even briefly for room.

concepts: Every TaskQueue implementation honours one contract: offer returns false when it cannot accept, poll returns null when empty, and null is rejected the same way by all.
